name: Panvel–Kanyakumari Highway
aka: Includes the Kochi–Kanyakumari stretch of the former NH 47
lanes: Varies from 2 to 6 lanes; major widening under way

timeline.event: Renumbered as NH 66, replacing the old NH 17 and part of the old NH 47
Large sections of the rebuilt, wider highway in Kerala open to traffic in phases

history: NH 66 hugs India's western coast from Panvel, just outside Mumbai, all the way to Kanyakumari at the country's southern tip. For most of its life it was known as NH 17, a winding two-lane road through the Konkan, Goa, coastal Karnataka and Kerala; the 2010 renumbering joined it with part of the old NH 47 to reach Kanyakumari. Since the late 2010s the highway has been rebuilt much wider, including a huge project to make the Kerala stretch a six-lane road, with large sections opening from 2025.
facts: Runs about 1,640 km along the Arabian Sea coast through five states.
Crosses dozens of rivers, estuaries and backwaters between the Western Ghats and the sea.
Runs roughly parallel to the Konkan Railway for much of its length.
Passes through Panaji, the capital of Goa.
The Kerala section is being rebuilt as a wide six-lane highway, one of the state's biggest infrastructure projects.

sources.title: NHAI — National Highways Authority of India
